# Plugin Portfolio Rethink — Roadmap

> Scope verified against live marketplace: 27 plugins in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and 27 dirs in `plugins/`. Central structural finding (verified by grep): **zero of 27 plugins declare any hook** — no `plugin.json` references hooks, and the only `PreToolUse`/`PreCompact` mentions in the tree are doc prose and lockfiles. The hook-event surface (PreToolUse, PreCompact, Stop, SessionStart) is completely unexploited. Ranking metric throughout: **demand × feasibility ÷ effort**, with feasibility downgraded for anything that fights an Anthropic platform limitation or a funded incumbent.

## Executive Summary

- **Open a "hooks tier."** The biggest untapped lever is mechanical enforcement via hooks — no plugin ships one today. The four highest-ROI new ideas (`aio-completion-gate`, `aio-secrets-guardrail`, `aio-claude-md-guardrails`, `aio-session-survival`) are all hook-first and each becomes a reusable reference for the rest of the portfolio. Ship one as a flagship, then template the rest.
- **Stand up a "security" category from nothing.** The portfolio has *knowledge* about security (aio-advisor's threat-models corpus) but **zero active security tooling**. `aio-secrets-guardrail`, `aio-skill-security-audit`, and `aio-deps-audit` are net-new, high-demand, and mutually reinforcing — but must stay separate plugins (different lifecycle trigger points).
- **Two slam-dunk extends beat most new plugins.** `aio-design-system` + a `wcag-audit` skill reuses an existing 7-file WCAG 2.2 corpus (verified at `aio-uiux/references/05-accessibility/`), and `aio-codeflow` + a `spec-contract` skill fills the verified gap between `aio-plan` (stops at plan) and execution. Both are S-effort, zero new marketplace entries.
- **Fix the review-trigger collision.** Three skills (`aio-code-review`, `aio-codeflow:aio-review-deep`, `aio-codeflow:aio-review-quick`) all fire on "review my PR." Split them into *playbook* vs *execution engine* triggers — this is a discoverability bug hurting the marketplace's most-requested workflow.
- **Split `aio-claude-toolkit`.** It bundles a version-fragile 6-skill binary-patching pipeline with 3 unrelated meta-skills (verified: 9 skills). The "toolkit" name hides a niche, brittle tool and three misfiled utilities. Extract the patch pipeline; reposition the meta-skills.
- **De-personalize the MCP supply chain.** Multiple plugins (`aio-devops`, `aio-saas-tools`, `aio-research`) route users to unpinned `nguyenvanduocit/*` personal forks installed via `go install @latest`. Lead with official CLIs (`gh`, `glab`) where ubiquitous, pin the rest. This is a maintenance single-point-of-failure across the catalog.
- **Reject the seductive-but-infeasible.** `aio-openapi-drift` (static differ is infeasible), `aio-staged-review`, `aio-rules-sync` (two of three pillars now native; incumbent + AGENTS.md convergence), and `aio-hooks-scaffolder` as a *standalone* (the pain is a one-turn ask) do not survive the reality lens.

## New Plugin Opportunities

Ranked by demand × feasibility ÷ effort.

### 1. aio-completion-gate — **demand 7, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** Claude claims "done/fixed/passing" while leaving TODOs/placeholders, skipping tests, and fabricating claims; persistent memory files become a confabulation amplifier where invented "facts" graduate to next-session ground truth. 96% distrust AI code but only 48% verify before committing. Audience: solo devs and teams who trust the "done" message.
- **Why #1:** It is a *mechanical interceptor*, not another playbook — the differentiator vs the existing advisory review plugins. It directly codifies the user's own CLAUDE.md "evidence over assertion / verify before claiming done" principle as enforceable policy. First-mover on the Stop-hook surface.
- **Evidence:** https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27430 (confabulation amplifier) · https://digitalscholarship.library.jhu.edu/s/aivoices/item/360 · https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47234917
- **Scope:** (1) Stop/SubagentStop hook scanning the working-tree diff for TODO/FIXME/stub/"not implemented" markers + done/fixed/passing language with no recorded test receipt → blocks completion demanding evidence; (2) configurable receipt mechanism running the project's real test/build command from `.claude/completion-gate.local.md`; (3) MEMORY.md verified-vs-unverified tagging script so unverified guesses can't silently become ground truth; (4) a skill documenting the receipt format + deliberate-bypass escape hatch (so users don't disable it under time pressure). Position explicitly against `aio-code-review` in the README: "interceptor, not playbook." Do NOT cite the dev.to "common issues" post — it doesn't support this pain.

### 2. aio-secrets-guardrail — **demand 7, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** AI agents leak secrets at ~2x baseline; scaffolded integrations commit hardcoded keys before governance exists; prompt-injection can exfiltrate secrets into public PR comments (Microsoft's Claude Code Action CVE). 28.6M secrets in public commits in 2025 (+34% YoY). Audience: all AI-agent users, especially teams wiring integrations/CI.
- **Why high:** The portfolio's first *active* security plugin; the untrusted-content half mirrors a real CVE class no other plugin addresses.
- **Evidence:** https://blog.gitguardian.com/local-guardrails-for-secrets-security
- **Scope:** (1) PreToolUse hook on `git commit|git push` + Write/Edit: shell out to gitleaks/trufflehog if present, fallback to a bundled high-signal pattern set (AWS, GitHub PATs, `sk-ant-*`, OpenAI `sk-*`, private-key blocks) + entropy heuristic; on hit, block with file:line and a move-to-env fix; include an allowlist/baseline so it isn't noise users disable. (2) UserPromptSubmit + PreToolUse untrusted-content guardrail: warn when the agent is about to act on issue/PR/comment/web text before reading `.env`/`~/.aws`/`/proc/self/environ` or pushing. Keep separate from `aio-deps-audit` — different lifecycle points; merging bloats both. Frame as a fast first-line guardrail, not a compliance guarantee.

### 3. aio-claude-md-guardrails — **demand 7 (provider-confirmed recurring), effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** Claude reads, acknowledges, then violates explicit CLAUDE.md rules by the 4th–5th interaction (used `cp` instead of Edit despite a rule stated 3x, broke production). Vague normative prose silently drops; bloated CLAUDE.md (>~200 lines) goes unread. Audience: all Claude Code users/teams relying on CLAUDE.md to enforce conventions.
- **Why high:** PreToolUse hooks are the only thing that fixes acknowledged-then-violated drift, and no marketplace plugin yet emits them. Differentiates cleanly from the existing `claude-md-management:claude-md-improver` (audit only) on the hook-emission path.
- **Evidence:** https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/15443 · https://aiweekender.substack.com/p/claude-code-keeps-forgetting-your
- **Scope:** Two skills. **guardrail-generator (headline):** parse NEVER/ALWAYS/protected-path rules from CLAUDE.md → emit `hooks.json` + PreToolUse scripts that deterministically block (`cp`/`mv` of code files, `rm -rf`, `git push --force`, edits to protected paths) with exit code 2. **claude-md-health (support):** flag length over the ~200-line threshold, prose that should be a hook (hand to skill 1), contradictions/duplicates; refactor a monolith into orchestrator-root + linked sub-files. Do NOT re-implement generic CLAUDE.md auditing.

### 4. aio-session-survival — **demand 8, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** Auto-compaction and `/compact` silently discard precise technical context (decisions, paths, failed approaches, the architectural "why") with no backup; `--resume` often starts fresh. Users lose multi-hour sessions and pay a 10–15 min re-orientation tax, hand-rolling bash snapshots of `~/.claude` `.jsonl` files. Audience: power users running long multi-day sessions.
- **Why strong demand but #4:** Highest raw demand (8), but honestly best-effort *mitigation*, not a lossless fix (Anthropic owns that) — feasibility capped, so it ranks just below the enforcement-grade gates. Still the cleanest demonstration of PreCompact + SessionStart hooks.
- **Evidence:** https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/43696 (resume starts fresh) · https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/25695 (requested handoff fields) · https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/43733 (PreCompact = shell only) · https://dev.to/gonewx/claude-code-lost-my-4-hour-session-heres-the-0-fix-that-actually-works-24h6
- **Scope:** (1) PreCompact hook (shell) snapshots the live `.jsonl` into `.claude/sessions/snapshots/<ts>.jsonl` + refreshes a handoff scaffold — be explicit in docs that the hook cannot author the rich narrative (shell only). (2) SessionStart hook emits the latest `handoff-*.md` as `additionalContext` to re-hydrate `--resume`. (3) `/checkpoint` skill: the authoring pass PreCompact can't do — writes the structured handoff (task+status, modified files, KEY ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS, FAILED APPROACHES, blockers, preferences). (4) `/restore`: list snapshots/handoffs, copy a `.jsonl` back, print `claude --resume <id>`. Position honestly as survival + mitigation. Zero-config, pure shell + markdown, paths via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.

### 5. aio-reliable-tests — **demand 8, effort M/L**
- **Pain + audience:** AI tests verify implementation not behavior (rename a var → break), test the framework itself, pick the wrong runner (Jasmine in a Jest project), over-mock, emit 40+ redundant tests, happy-path only. Negative/edge/auth-failure testing with data factories is the recognized differentiator the portfolio lacks. Audience: frontend/backend/QA teams letting Claude generate tests.
- **Why high but effort-heavier:** Demand 8 and net-new, but god-skill risk pushes effort to M/L; needs careful sub-skill splitting.
- **Evidence:** https://dev.to/alfredoperez/create-reliable-unit-tests-with-claude-code-4e8p · https://qaskills.sh/blog/best-claude-code-skills-for-automated-testing · https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47234917
- **Scope (hybrid):** (1) framework-detection script reading package.json/jest/vitest/angular.json/go.mod — refuses to write until it confirms the existing runner+assertion style (kills Jasmine-in-Jest); (2) documented rule-set: behavior-over-implementation, ban framework-tautology tests, a mock budget + max-tests-per-file cap as pre-write checklist and post-write linter; (3) negative/edge/auth-failure generator with data-factory templates (the differentiator); (4) run+self-repair loop on the detected command, capped iterations; (5) redundancy-pruner reporting coverage delta before deleting near-dupes. Cross-link `aio-advisor` (strategic testing-strategies) and `aio-golang-mastery` (Go testing) as complementary, not duplicated. Consider splitting pruner/flaky-detector into sibling skills.

### 6. aio-migration-safety — **demand 8, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** AI DB migrations produce unsafe SQL (NOT NULL without default, dropping in-use columns, non-CONCURRENT index builds on large tables) that takes prod down for hours. Zero migration-safety tooling in the portfolio. Audience: backend/full-stack teams on Postgres/MySQL with AI-written migrations.
- **Why high:** Production-down stakes, recurring, net-new. Plays to the LLM's strength (context reasoning) rather than re-implementing mature deterministic linters.
- **Evidence:** https://dev.to/myougatheaxo/database-migrations-with-claude-code-safe-schema-changes-without-breaking-production-4eg1
- **Scope (hybrid):** (1) hazard-catalog SKILL.md (each entry: unsafe form, why it locks/rewrites, safe expand/contract rewrite); (2) lint script auto-detecting framework (Prisma/knex/alembic/golang-migrate) flagging deterministic patterns; (3) the differentiator — a context-reasoning workflow that greps the codebase for column usage before approving a DROP, asks about table size/traffic, and sequences expand/contract + backfill + feature-flag deploys; (4) emit-CI-guard pre-deploy step. Credit strong_migrations, safe-ecto, Squawk as prior art. Frame as Postgres/MySQL OLTP, distinct from `aio-starrocks` (OLAP).

### 7. aio-skill-security-audit — **demand 7, effort M/L**
- **Pain + audience:** Claude Code skills/agents are an unaudited supply chain — `!`-prefixed dynamic-context commands run before the LLM sees them, `allowed-tools: Bash(*)` and `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` override user settings, hijacked SessionStart hooks re-execute. Audience: power users/teams installing community skills/plugins/marketplaces.
- **Evidence:** https://labs.reversec.com/posts/2026/05/skill-issues-compromising-claude-code-with-malicious-skills-agents-part-1
- **Scope:** Deterministic scanner parsing YAML frontmatter of every SKILL.md/agent.md/settings.json/plugin.json — flag with severity+file:line: `!`-prefixed commands, `Bash(*)`/wildcard tools, `bypassPermissions`, SessionStart/PreToolUse/pre/postinstall hooks invoking shell, network-egress patterns (curl/wget/nc/`/dev/tcp`), base64/eval obfuscation, remote fetch-and-exec. Plus an LLM triage pass over prose for coercive/secrecy/manipulation language (the 84% of threats the scanner can't catch). Output a quarantined risk report — "here is what installing this grants" — framed as risk surface, NOT a safety guarantee, never "all clear." Seed rules from arXiv 2602.06547, SafeDep IoCs, CVE-2025-59536.

### 8. aio-deps-audit — **demand 7, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** CVE auditing is slow/noisy/skipped under deadline; the disclosure-to-patch window is where supply-chain attacks live, now acute as malicious npm packages backdoor Claude Code via hijacked SessionStart hooks. Audience: solo devs and security-conscious teams across npm/pip/cargo/go.
- **Evidence:** Re-center on Mend/safedep.io/StepSecurity advisories (Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud / Miasma IOCs). Drop the unsubstantiated dev.to citation.
- **Scope:** (1) thin orchestration skill wrapping `osv-scanner` (cross-ecosystem, reachability prioritization where supported) — do NOT reimplement scanning; (2) the UNIQUE core — a manifest/install-hook auditor flagging malicious pre/post-install scripts, hijacked `.claude/settings.json` SessionStart hooks, suspicious `.vscode/tasks.json` folderOpen triggers; (3) safe upgrade-path suggestions. Position as "detect supply-chain backdoors that target your AI coding agent." Verified non-overlap: `aio-golang-mastery` is Go-only govulncheck; `aio-advisor:aio-threat-models` is knowledge-only.

### 9. aio-token-budget — **demand 7, effort M**
- **Pain + audience:** No usage visibility for Pro/Max users; a single command spawns 8–12 internal calls (30k+ tokens); an unnoticed `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` silently bills API rates (documented 93% cost blowups). Audience: cost-conscious solo devs and Pro/Max teams hitting limits.
- **Evidence:** https://www.truefoundry.com/blog/claude-code-limits-explained · https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/claude-code-pricing/ · https://www.aol.com/articles/claude-code-users-hitting-usage-115924704.html
- **Scope (two tiers):** **Tier 1 (easy, high-confidence):** script parsing `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` usage objects → attribution report by tool/file/subagent/MCP server + cache-hit rate + $ estimate. Differentiator vs ccusage: ccusage *aggregates*, this *attributes what ate the budget*. **Tier 2 (the moat):** PreToolUse hook detecting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` override (this single check may justify the plugin) + redundant full-file re-reads; Stop/threshold hook surfacing cumulative burn vs the weekly window. Externalize the price table (prices drift); pull current model-id/pricing from the `claude-api` skill rather than hardcoding. SKILL.md line: "ccusage tells you what you spent yesterday; aio-token-budget tells you what's eating your budget right now and stops the footguns before they bill you."

### 10. aio-skill-doctor — **demand 6, effort M (v1) / L (v2)**
- **Pain + audience:** Skills fail silently — combined descriptions overflow the ~15k-char SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET and get dropped; vague descriptions never fire (~50% activation unoptimized). An audit of 214 skills found 73% scored below 60/100. Audience: plugin/skill authors and power users. This marketplace's own 27-plugin quality bar is the canary user.
- **Evidence:** https://dev.to/thestack_ai/i-audited-214-claude-code-skills-73-were-silently-broken-2m9a · https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/21947 · https://medium.com/@ivan.seleznov1/why-claude-code-skills-dont-activate-and-how-to-fix-it-86f679409af1
- **Scope (differentiators only — the linter space is saturated):** (1) **budget-attribution script** summing all installed descriptions vs the char budget, predicting which skills get silently dropped (strongest unique angle; built-ins only warn, none attribute per-skill); (2) directive-rewrite skill converting passive statements into imperative "invoke when…" with 4–6 verb synonyms front-loaded; (3) 14-criteria health score mirroring the public rubric; (4) opt-in v2 trigger-probe harness reporting empirical activation %. Acknowledge the startup warning exists — position as the diagnosis+fix layer it lacks.

## Revise / Extend Existing Plugins

Ranked by demand × feasibility ÷ effort. Top two are S-effort, no new marketplace entry.

### 1. aio-design-system — add `wcag-audit` skill (S, demand 7) — TOP EXTEND
Verified: `aio-uiux/references/05-accessibility/` already holds a 7-file WCAG 2.2 corpus (wcag-22-essential-guide, aria-patterns, keyboard-navigation, screen-reader, color-motion, form-accessibility, testing-checklist). The marketplace covers aesthetics + visual-diff but has **no a11y audit**. Add a skill that: runs axe-core against live DOM via the existing Chrome DevTools MCP + eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y for static/CI; reuses the corpus for WCAG 2.2 AA violation mapping; ships **baseline-diff mode** (report only NEW regressions — mirrors `aio-visual-diff` philosophy, the differentiator free competitors lack); auto-fix pass for ARIA/contrast/focus/RTL; SARIF output for CI parity. Bump `aio-design-system` minor. **Evidence:** https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents

### 2. aio-codeflow — add `spec-contract` skill (S/M, demand 7)
Verified: `aio-codeflow/skills/` has `aio-plan` but no contract/verify step — it stops at the plan. Underspecification is the real agentic-coding bottleneck. Add a `spec-contract` skill: (1) lightweight Socratic interview (3–5 questions, reuse the deep-interview pattern) crystallizing Architecture / Constraints / Invariants / Success-Acceptance-Criteria into one committed `docs/spec-contracts/{feature}.md`; (2) post-codegen verify-against-contract step checking the diff/tests against each acceptance criterion → pass/fail gate (the differentiator from both `aio-plan` and spec-kit). Insert in the chain: discover → map → plan → SPEC-CONTRACT → execute → verify. Differentiate from spec-kit by being a drop-in skill, not a project-bootstrap framework. Bump `aio-codeflow`, no new marketplace entry. **Evidence:** https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46125341

### 3. aio-code-review + aio-codeflow review skills — disambiguate triggers (S, high relevance)
Three skills collide on "review my PR": `aio-code-review` (judgment playbook), `aio-codeflow:aio-review-deep` (multi-agent engine), `aio-codeflow:aio-review-quick` (change-detection). They're complementary but a fuzzy-match router can't tell. Sharpen `aio-code-review` toward judgment/authoring triggers ("how should I review", "is this approvable", "write a CL description", "handle pushback", "lgtm threshold") and let review-deep/quick own "run a review for me." Add a one-line cross-reference in each. Keep all three — the playbook is orthogonal to the engines.

### 4. aio-workflow — add `aio-orchestration-survival` skill (M, demand 6)
Verified: `aio-workflow` has only `aio-workflow-creator`. Add a second skill targeting three verified multi-agent pains as runnable patterns: (1) **overflow-safe fan-out** — each subagent writes full output to a run-dir file and returns `{path, summary, status}`; recovery script scraping completed `<result>` blocks from `.jsonl` after a "Prompt is too long" crash (issue #23463); (2) **worktree conflict-guard** — per-agent file-ownership manifest + pre-merge same-file overlap detector + safe sequential merge ordering; (3) **unattended preflight** — command allowlist + fail-fast + per-phase checkpoints for overnight runs (issue #27172). **Caveats before building:** drop/re-cite the mislabeled #43733; the Task `run_in_background` gap (#9905) is an Anthropic limitation — teach the documented Workflow-tool concurrent-agent-pool workaround, don't imply the plugin adds async to native Task. Bias to scripts over prose (the existing skill is already 297 dense lines). **Evidence:** https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/23463 · https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27172 · https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/parallel-agentic-development-claude-code-worktrees

### 5. aio-devops — de-personalize github/gitlab (M, high relevance)
Verified: `aio-github/SKILL.md` warns "This is github-mcp, NOT the official gh CLI" and requires `go install` of `nguyenvanduocit/github-mcp`. In mid-2026 `gh`/`glab` and the official GitHub MCP are ubiquitous; the fork's tool surface is a strict subset of `gh`. Revise both skills to lead with official CLIs + official GitHub MCP, demote (or drop) the personal forks to optional fallback. Removes the `go install` prerequisite and the maintenance SPOF. Keep `aio-worktree` (optionally split out, but bundling is fine if reframed as "git + forge workflows").

Verified: 9 skills — 6 patch-* (binary-patching pipeline, version-fragile; `aio-patch-anchor` exists solely for drift recovery on Claude version bumps) + 3 misfiled meta (`aio-skillify`, `aio-feedback`, `aio-dream`). Extract the 6 patch-* skills into a dedicated `aio-claude-patch` so its niche, version-fragile nature is honestly scoped. Keep `aio-feedback` (marketplace-specific). `aio-skillify`/`aio-dream` duplicate native OMC skillify/learner/wiki — keep with a note for portable non-OMC users or fold into a small `aio-claude-meta`. Verified architecture staleness (not frontmatter): scaffolds a two-process Vite(3000)→Bun(3001) proxy under PM2. Keep `aio-atlassian` + `aio-google-workspace` (broad, durable). Add an X API access-tier caveat to `aio-x` (paywall/429 reality). Flag or drop `aio-tanca` (single Vietnamese HR SaaS, near-zero general relevance). Pin the `nguyenvanduocit/*` install versions.

### 10. aio-image — fix container framing (S, high relevance)
The plugin is named broad `aio-image` but ships only `aio-remove-background`. Lowest-effort fix: tighten the plugin description's first clause to lead with "background removal / image matting" so fuzzy discovery matches intent. ## Consolidate / Deprecate

- **SPLIT `aio-claude-toolkit` → `aio-claude-patch`** (6 patch-* skills) + keep `aio-feedback` + reposition `aio-skillify`/`aio-dream`. The "toolkit" name is a catch-all hiding a brittle binary-patcher and three unrelated meta utilities (verified 9 skills, two unrelated concerns).
- **DO NOT MERGE the security trio.** `aio-secrets-guardrail` (commit-time), `aio-deps-audit` (CVE/install-hook), `aio-skill-security-audit` (skill supply chain) trigger at different lifecycle points — keep three plugins under a shared "security" category; merging bloats each.
- **DO NOT MERGE `aio-monitoring-observability` into `aio-devops`.** Distinct concerns (metrics/SLO/tracing vs git/forge plumbing) — verified no material overlap.
- **DO NOT MERGE `aio-advisor`'s advisor/reference split.** The guided-vs-encyclopedia split (effort medium vs low) is intentional and defensible.
- **FOLD `aio-context-auditor` into `aio-claude-toolkit` (as a sibling skill, not a standalone plugin).** It's a Claude-config maintenance concern that colocates with existing config tooling; a standalone 28th plugin to fix plugin-bloat is self-ironic. (demand 7) Scope: audit script ranking MCP-server/tool/plugin token cost (GitHub MCP = 55k tokens; multi-MCP burns 66k–82k of the 200k window empty), unused-plugin detector vs the 4–6 rule, scoped-profile generator. Keep low-footprint (markdown + on-demand script). **Evidence:** https://scottspence.com/posts/optimising-mcp-server-context-usage-in-claude-code · https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/claude-code-mcp-server-token-overhead
- **RELOCATE `aio-codeflow:aio-rubber-duck`** next to `aio-catch-me-up` in a small "learn/think" grouping. It's a thinking aid, not a code-flow stage, and its "help me understand" triggers collide with `aio-catch-me-up`. Boundary: understanding finished AI work = catch-me-up; thinking through an unsolved problem aloud = rubber-duck.
- **DEPRECATION WATCH (not kill yet):** `aio-tanca` (org-specific niche), `aio-research-kit` (competes with native deep-research), `aio-gherkin-refine` (softening demand — broaden framing to "requirements→acceptance-criteria" rather than deprecate). `aio-epub-translate` and the `aio-saas-tools`/`aio-research` MCP wrappers carry proprietary/personal-service dependency risk — keep but surface the dependency prominently.

## Triggering & Discoverability Fixes

Verified portfolio note: per the audit, every existing SKILL.md scored "strong" on trigger quality — the issues are **collisions and container-name mismatches**, not weak keyword sets.

- **Review collision (highest priority):** `aio-code-review` vs `aio-codeflow:aio-review-deep`/`aio-review-quick` all fire on "review my PR." Re-weight as playbook vs engine (see Revise #3).
- **Understanding collision:** `aio-catch-me-up` vs `aio-codeflow:aio-rubber-duck` both claim "help me understand / walk me through." Strip rubber-duck's "help me understand" so catch-me-up owns post-build understanding (see Relocate above).
- **Advisor vs reference:** `aio-advisor` — add "design from scratch / which approach" weight to advisor and "explain / what is" to reference so the router disambiguates (low priority; already mostly there).
- **Container-name mismatch:** `aio-image` plugin name promises a toolkit, ships one tool — lead the description with "background removal / matting" (see Revise #10).
- **Registry vs SKILL.md drift:** `aio-youtube` marketplace.json description ("Search YouTube and extract video transcripts using yt-dlp") is thinner than its SKILL.md frontmatter. Enrich the marketplace entry for consistency. Audit all 27 marketplace descriptions against SKILL.md frontmatter for the same drift.
- **Dataviz routing:** add a one-line cross-reference in `aio-uiux`'s Data Visualization Colors section pointing chart/dashboard questions to `aio-dashboard-design`.
- **For all new plugins:** front-load imperative "invoke when…" trigger phrases with 4–6 verb synonyms (the `aio-skill-doctor` remediation pattern) — especially the hook plugins whose value is invisible until they fire.

## Gaps Still Open

The critic flagged these missing categories with verified zero coverage (grep-confirmed: incidental hits only). They need more demand research before committing build effort — ranked by likely AI-codegen pain:

1. **CI/CD pipeline authoring & debugging** (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI YAML) — `aio-devops` is git-operation-level only; verified zero hits for the workflow-YAML authoring/debugging surface ("why is my Action red", caching, matrix, OIDC, reusable workflows). The #1 place AI config silently breaks. Research: "Claude Code github actions debugging", "act local actions testing".
2. **Container & IaC authoring/safety** (Dockerfile/Compose/K8s/Terraform/Pulumi) — only incidental mentions; no write/lint/secure capability (multi-stage slimming, non-root, image CVE scan, `terraform plan` diff review, drift detection, kubeconform). Top AI-codegen risk (root images, destructive applies). Research: "AI generated Dockerfile insecure", "terraform plan review AI", "IaC drift detection".
3. **App-level performance & profiling** — `aio-starrocks` tunes DB queries, `aio-monitoring` covers prod SLOs, but nothing for CPU/flamegraph, memory leaks, allocation analysis, bundle-size, Big-O/N+1 regression. Verified zero hits. Research: "pprof flamegraph workflow", "memory leak debugging LLM", "N+1 detection in AI code".
4. **Load/stress/chaos/fuzz/property-based testing** — `aio-reliable-tests` (proposed) is unit-scoped; non-functional testing (k6/locust, chaos, fuzzing, property-based) is a distinct uncovered category that catches concurrency/scale bugs unit tests never will. Research: "k6 load test scripting", "property-based testing adoption".
5. **i18n/l10n engineering** (distinct from translation) — `aio-epub-translate` translates content; nothing extracts hardcoded strings, handles ICU MessageFormat/pluralization/RTL, or catches missing translation keys at build. AI agents routinely hardcode user-facing strings. Research: "AI hardcoded strings i18n extraction", "missing translation key detection".
6. **HTTP/API client & runtime contract testing** — `aio-browser-cookie` grabs cookies, `aio-saas-tools` wraps specific SaaS; no general `.http`/REST-client workflow, request collections, or contract tests against a running service. Devs constantly need to exercise the API the agent just built. Research: ".http rest client file", "contract test against running service".
7. **Developer onboarding / repo ramp-up for humans** — `aio-codeflow` maps code, `aio-catch-me-up` teaches what an agent did, but neither generates a newcomer onboarding doc / dev-env bootstrap / "where do I start" walkthrough. Research: "AI codebase onboarding doc generation", "dev environment bootstrap reproducibility".
8. **Release engineering** (semver bump, changelog/release-notes, tagging, GitHub releases, monorepo version coordination) — entirely absent, and **this repo itself manually bumps plugin.json versions** (a friction its own CLAUDE.md documents). Dogfood candidate. Research: "AI changelog from conventional commits", "changesets/semantic-release workflow".
9. **Android & cross-platform mobile + browser E2E** — `aio-ios-device-debug` is iOS-only; no Android (adb/logcat), React Native/Flutter, or E2E flow authoring (Playwright/Cypress generation — `aio-visual-diff` measures CSS but doesn't drive flows). Mobile is a large segment left half-covered. Research: "android adb logcat debugging", "Playwright test generation pain".

## Rejected Ideas

Kept honest — these did not survive the demand × feasibility ÷ effort lens:

- **aio-openapi-drift (the static spec-vs-handler differ)** — *Infeasible as proposed.* A reliable static differ across arbitrary frameworks is the hard problem; the honest re-scope (a CI-integration playbook wiring oasdiff/Spectral/Schemathesis) is lower-novelty and overlaps the proposed CI/IaC gap and `aio-devops`. Deprioritize unless there's direct evidence of repeated Claude-Code-specific demand for API-contract wiring. Evidence: https://apitect.com/blogs/stopping-schema-drift-how-to-keep-your-openapi-spec-and-code-in-sync-automatically
- **aio-rules-sync (standalone)** — *Mostly self-solving + funded incumbent.* Two of three pillars are native (AGENTS.md interop via `@import`/symlink; cross-tool ingestion via `/init`; auto-memory + `/memory`). The one uncovered slice (generating `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`/Windsurf/Copilot derivatives + drift detection) lives outside Claude Code, faces agentrulegen (funded), and is being obsoleted by AGENTS.md convergence (60k+ repos). If pursued at all: a minimal `sync-rules` script folded into `aio-claude-toolkit`, framed as a transitional bridge.
- **aio-hooks-scaffolder (standalone)** — *Pain is a one-turn agent ask.* The only durable nuggets (the PostToolUse formatter infinite-loop guard + a toolchain→hook cheat sheet) belong as a reference inside `claude-code-setup`'s automation-recommender, not a new plugin. The cited synergy rationale depended on two plugins that don't exist.
- **aio-setup-advisor** — *Weakly-sourced curation half.* The which-primitive-when decision matrix is well-evidenced, but the 4–6 plugin / 30-day pruning "rule" rests on a single source (bswen) and shouldn't be marketed as consensus. If built, lead with the decision matrix + a scaffolder-with-trigger-self-check, de-emphasize the curation numbers, and **verify against the existing `claude-automation-recommender` skill first** to avoid duplicating the recommender half. Net: deprioritize below the hook tier.
- **aio-code-review (adversarial-self-review skill)** — *Not novel* (per the discovery's rejected list); covered by existing review skills.
- **aio-document-data** — *Not novel.*
- **aio-lsp** — *Not novel*; LSP capability is already provided by the harness/OMC and `aio-codeflow`'s LSP-bound skills.
- **aio-staged-review** — *Not feasible.*
